name: Monastir Habib Bourguiba International Airport
before:
The resort airport for Monastir and Sousse, and the arrival point for Monastir-Skanes and Port El Kantaoui. Almost all of its charter flying is concentrated in the tourist season, with Nouvelair and Tunisair the main carriers.

The traffic figures tell a clear story. The airport led Tunisia with 4,279,802 passengers in 2007, was down to 1.586 million by 2019 and 420,000 in 2021, and has climbed back steadily since to 1.6 million in 2024. Against a terminal rated for 3.5 million a year, that leaves plenty of room.

The train is a genuine advantage here. The airport is on the electrified Sahel Metro line between Sousse and Monastir, so a client can reach either town by rail rather than by coach.

The airport opened in 1968 and has been run by TAV Airports Holding since 2008, on rights that run to May 2047.

It is named after Habib Bourguiba, the former president, who was born in Monastir.
after:
The resort airport for Monastir and Sousse. Its traffic is concentrated in the tourist season, and Nouvelair and Tunisair both fly here.

The airport handled 1.586 million passengers in 2019, fell to 420,000 in 2021 and has climbed back steadily since, to 1.6 million in 2024. Against a capacity of about 3.5 million a year, that leaves plenty of room.

The train is a genuine advantage here. Trains on the electrified Sahel Metro line stop at the airport, between Sousse and Monastir, so a client can reach either town by rail rather than by coach.

The airport opened in 1968 and has been run by TAV Airports Holding since 2008, on rights that run to May 2047.

It is named after Habib Bourguiba.
